title: [Peek] Black, click-through rectangle stays on screen after closing the preview

judgment.rationale: The strongest lead is a preview child visibility/lifetime mismatch, not a proven driver or DWM defect. Reproduce the close path before approving a repair; do not repeat the bot's generic ZIP request.
evidence: The report gives Esc/X close steps and native-window observations: hidden main window, visible DesktopChildSiteBridge and layered PeekShellPreviewHandlerContainer matching the artifact.
The problem happened twice near dwm.exe restarts; causation is not established. NVIDIA and a virtual display driver are listed.
Killing Peek UI removes the rectangle. Existing screenshots and detailed window evidence are sufficient for an initial maintainer reproduction.

Upstream main 9e6593c34949: src/modules/peek/Peek.FilePreviewer/Controls/ShellPreviewHandlerControl.xaml.cs: The control owns an IPreviewHandler, HandlerVisibility, and a native PeekShellPreviewHandlerContainer; inspect their close/visibility sequencing together.

fix_assessment.rationale: Conditional lightweight proposal, not an implementation-grade design. Native-window evidence points to the container; no maintainer reproduction or failing call is established.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve preview-child visibility on close
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A shell preview child may remain composited after its parent is hidden; the report localizes the surface but does not identify the failing close transition.
plan: Reproduce and record parent/child visibility at the reported close transition.
If the container survives, make hide/unload idempotent at the owning preview lifecycle boundary rather than changing graphics drivers.
Add close/reopen coverage for shell-handler and non-shell previews.
verification: No black surface after Esc/X, repeated previews or a recoverable compositor reset.
Preview reopen and keyboard focus continue to work.

confidence.rationale: Native-window evidence points to the container; no maintainer reproduction or failing call is established.
